problem: BRAIN failed after the pricing visibility fix because three legacy tests matched the old one-line hidden-property implementation instead of the stronger visible-state contract.
root_cause: The regression suite encoded incidental source syntax rather than the behavioral invariant. The implementation correctly evolved to an active-state tuple including hidden, style.display, aria-hidden, class and tabIndex, but stale regexes treated that improvement as a failure.
prevention: Pricing interaction tests assert the complete visible-state semantics, not an obsolete source-code spelling.
Lifecycle and plan-group regressions must require hidden plus inline display plus aria-hidden state.
Test contracts must evolve in the same lineage when implementation semantics are intentionally strengthened.
Production browser proof remains authoritative over source regex markers.
